p:cNvPr.descr: A schematic that shows the lactose metabolism of E. coli. The entire process occurs in a yellow background, labeled as cytoplasm. The cytoplasm is outlined by a darker yellow border, sandwiched by two light blues lines; this is labeled the plasma membrane. The white space at the top of the plasma membrane is labeled as extracellular space. In the middle of the plasma membrane is a small, purple folded structure, labeled as galactoside (lactose) permease, that has an arrow passing through it; the arrow is labeled as lactose and is shown entering the cytoplasm. From the top of the cytoplasm, where lactose enters, there are two identical elongated hexagons with the three bottom sides shaded deeply. To the top right of the hexagons, both have a O, and to the top left, they have a CH2OH that bonds down to an H (on the inside). To the bottom left, both have an OH (on the inside) that bonds down to H, and to the bottom right, they have an H (on the inside) that bonds down to OH. The middle left and right points is where these two structures differ. The structure on the right has an OH that bonds down to H at the middle right point, and on the middle left point, it has an H that bonds down to an O. The O on this structure also bonds up to an H on the second structure. The middle left point of the second structure has an OH that bonds down to an H. Below these two structures is a deeply-shaded line labeled beta-galactosidase in blue. The line branches into two curved arrows, one to the left (shaded deeply) that shows H2O curving into the arrow, labeled hydrolysis, and one to the right (a slightly lighter shade of black) labeled isomerization. The hydrolysis arrow points down to galactose, which is represented by the first hexagon structure described at the beginning, with an OH that bonds down to H on the middle right point, [plus] glucose below it, which is represented by a similar hexagon structure, but this time, an H bonds down to HO on the middle left point. The isomerization arrow to the right points down to allolactose, which is represented by an elongated hexagon with deeply shaded bottom sides, with an O at the top right, a CH2OH bonded down to an H (on the inside) to the top left, an HO bonded down to an H at the middle left point, an OH (on the inside) bonded down to an H at the bottom left point, an H (on the inside) bonded down to an OH at the bottom right point, and an O bonded down to an H at the middle right point. This same O bonds right to CH2, which bonds up to H (on the inside) of another hexagon with the three top sides shaded deeply. To the right of this point on the hexagon is an O. The middle right point has an H that bonds down to OH, the top right point has an OH that bonds down to an H (on the inside), the top left point has an H that bonds down to an OH (on the inside), and the top left point has an OH that bonds down to H.
